subject: Privatelink residency acknowledgement + CSQA intake for MedSecure
messages:
From: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medsecure.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai
Cc: compliance@medsecure.com, adam.liao@medsecure.com
Date: Sun, 25 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Residency confirmation + privatelink/peering checklist request

Hi Priyom,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we move toward a pilot I need to collect a short package for our security team (they call it CSQA intake). Can you confirm the following for Redwood when running in a Private deployment for MedSecure in the US region?

- Can you confirm that tenant compute and model serving will remain in the us-east-1 region and that no model artifacts or inference logs are replicated to other regions by default?
- Is there a standard PrivateLink (or equivalent) peering runbook and an expected IP range for firewall whitelisting?
- We’ll need a filtered CAIQ slice and SOC 2 summary (high level is fine) that maps to data residency controls and key management boundaries.
- Any specific requirements for customer-managed KMS integration (bring-your-own-key) and operator access?

Can you share an initial evidence bundle and a short mutual action plan (MAP) so I can get this into our procurement folder? We’re aiming to onboard a pilot by mid-November.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — copying our compliance lead (compliance@medsecure.com) and infra (adam.liao@medsecure.com).

Best,
Jessica Liu
Sr. Security Program Manager
MedSecure Health

Attachment: none (initial ask)
From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 26 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + privatelink/peering checklist request

Jessica — thanks for the clear list. Assigning Kimberley and Marissa to help pull the artifacts and draft the MAP. Quick answers up front:

- Residency: Yes — for a Redwood Private deployment we can pin tenant serving to a single cloud region (us-east-1). By default we do not replicate inference requests or model weights to other regions unless a customer explicitly enables multi-region replication. We will provide a formal statement and operational runbook snippet.

- Private connectivity: We have a PrivateLink-equivalent peering process. I’ll attach our runbook and an example whitelisting CSV (IP ranges are per-cluster and documented in the runbook).

- Evidence: Attaching a filtered CAIQ slice scoped to residency & networking, and a SOC2 summary that highlights control families relevant to tenancy isolation and key management.

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys (BYOK). Operator access to customer keys is limited; we will include the operator control flow and an HSM/KMS partitioning note.

Next steps:
1) I’ll upload the runbook and evidence bundle (see attachments).
2) Kimberley will propose a short MAP with milestones for a pilot peering test (whitelist -> test -> canary -> production).
3) Can you confirm who will own firewall rules on your side (security or infra)?

Proposed 30-min call to review on Wed 10/27 11:00am ET — does that work for your team?

—Priyom
Priyom Das
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: redwood_privatelink_runbook_v1.pdf; peering-ip-range.csv; caaiq_slice_medsecure.xlsx; soc2-2025-summary.pdf
From: Adam Liao <adam.liao@medsecure.com>
To: priyom.das@redwood.ai, kimberly.park@redwood.ai
Cc: Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medsecure.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 27 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + privatelink/peering checklist request

Thanks — confirmed the time for Wed 10/27 11:00am ET. A few clarifications ahead of the call:

- Firewall ownership: infra team will own the actual ACLs but security will provide the formal change ticket.
- For the IP ranges: can you indicate which ranges are for cluster control-plane vs data-plane? We typically only whitelist data-plane ranges.
- For BYOK: we need to confirm if Redwood operators can ever export or wrap keys on behalf of the customer. If not, please state that explicitly.

Also can you add an item to the MAP for an evidence handoff (signed PDF manifest that lists the included artifacts) so our procurement can link it to the PO? Finally — we’ll need a DocuSign signature on the Pilot Appendix (I can send a draft).

Appreciate it — looking forward to the call.

—Adam
Adam Liao
Cloud Infra Lead, MedSecure

From: priyom.das@redwood.ai
To: Adam Liao <adam.liao@medsecure.com>, Jessica Liu <jessica.liu@medsecure.com>
Cc: kimberly.park@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 28 Oct 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Residency confirmation + privatelink/peering checklist request

Adam/Jessica — thanks for the clarifications and for confirming the call. Recap and actions from our side:

1) Evidence bundle (attached): redwood_privatelink_runbook_v1.pdf, caaiq_slice_medsecure.xlsx, soc2-2025-summary.pdf, peering-ip-range.csv. The CAIQ slice highlights controls in A.5 (Data residency), A.12 (Network protection) and key management notes mapped to SOC 2 control families.

2) IP ranges: the attached peering-ip-range.csv includes a column labeled plane_type with values data-plane or control-plane. For pilot whitelisting you only need the data-plane rows; we’ve highlighted them in the CSV.

3) BYOK operator policy: Redwood operators cannot extract customer keys or export them. We provide a wrap/unwrap flow for HSM-backed keys and an audit trail; operator actions that involve key material are gated by a ticketed, logged process. We’ve summarized this on page 6 of the runbook.

4) MAP (proposed milestones):
   - Day 0: mutual signature of Pilot Appendix (DocuSign) -> procurement
   - Day 1–3: firewall whitelisting (MedSecure infra) -> verify connectivity
   - Day 4: canary inference test (small traffic) -> smoke checks for latency/egress
   - Day 7: expanded pilot load and SOC-ops review -> move to steady state

5) Evidence handoff: I will create a signed PDF manifest after you confirm the exact pilot appendix you want us to sign. If you send the DocuSign link, we’ll complete signature within 24 hours of legal review.

Next immediate asks for you: confirm the DocuSign link for the Pilot Appendix and the point-of-contact who will raise the firewall change ticket.

Thanks — copying Kimberley and Marissa for any supplementary artifacts.

—Priyom
